title: Global sections of the derived internal Hom
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site whose underlying category is small and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$; let $D(\mathcal O)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\Gamma(\mathcal C,-)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O,-)$ the global sections functor. For $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ put $H^0(\mathcal C,K)=H^0(\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal J^\bullet))$ for a K-injective complex $\mathcal J^\bullet$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] representing $K$ (one exists by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; the result does not depend on the choice up to canonical isomorphism, as two K-injective complexes representing $K$ are homotopy equivalent). Then for $L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
 H^0\bigl(\mathcal C,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)\bigr)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(L,M),
$$

with $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}$ the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: Lemma 08JA (sites-cohomology-lemma-section-RHom-over-U), the global statement; its proof uses Lemma 0A94 (sites-cohomology-lemma-RHom-into-K-injective) and the lemma sites-cohomology-lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective

proof.text: Choose a K-flat complex L^\bullet representing L [def-pc-kflat-complex]; one exists by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], which gives a K-flat resolution L^\bullet\to L_0^\bullet of any complex L_0^\bullet representing L. Choose a K-injective complex I^\bullet representing M; one exists by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By the definition of the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] (its last clause, any K-injective complex quasi-isomorphic to the second argument and any representative of the first), R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M) is represented, canonically up to isomorphism, by \mathcal Hom^\bullet(L^\bullet,I^\bullet); a change of the representatives L^\bullet, I^\bullet induces a quasi-isomorphism of these Hom complexes by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined]. Since L^\bullet is K-flat and I^\bullet is K-injective, \mathcal Hom^\bullet(L^\bullet,I^\bullet) is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. Hence it is an admissible choice of \mathcal J^\bullet in the definition of H^0(\mathcal C,-) in the statement, and H^0(\mathcal C,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M))=H^0(\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L^\bullet,I^\bullet))).

source.place: Lemma 08JA, proof: K-flat L, K-injective I, and sites-cohomology-lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective

proof.text: Apply \Gamma(\mathcal C,-)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O,-) degreewise. By the definition of the Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] (products and sheaf Hom computed sectionwise), a global section of \mathcal Hom^n(L^\bullet,I^\bullet) is a family of \mathcal O-linear maps f^p:L^p\to I^{p+n}; equivalently, this is the degree-n case of the tensor-Hom bijection \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O,\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L^p,I^{p+n}))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathcal O}L^p,I^{p+n})=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L^p,I^{p+n}) with K=\mathcal O (evaluate at the section 1). The differential is d_I\circ f-(-1)^n f\circ d_L, so \Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L^\bullet,I^\bullet)) is the Hom complex of abelian groups of L^\bullet and I^\bullet. Its H^0 consists of chain maps L^\bullet\to I^\bullet (the 0-cocycles) modulo null-homotopic ones (the 0-coboundaries d(h), h of degree -1), i.e. \operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(L^\bullet,I^\bullet). Since I^\bullet is K-injective, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] (with \mathcal A=\Mod(\mathcal O)) identifies this bijectively with \operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(L,M). With Step 1 this gives H^0(\mathcal C,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(L,M).

The bijection in Step 2 is the required canonical isomorphism. For a quasi-isomorphism of either representative, the map on Hom complexes is the one in [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined]; composing chain maps and passing to homotopy classes commutes with the localization map in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Thus the isomorphism is unchanged under representative replacements, and the same commuting-composition calculation proves naturality in L and M.
